title: The comparison: the main estimate

headline.label: Main estimate, the gap on the common output
headline.definition: the difference between the two sides' gross one-time wealth tax revenue once both are estimated on one definition, explained one disputed input at a time: BSZ Table 5 row 1 minus the NBER expected revenue

layers.name: The number on the page
layers.what: This layer is the root page's own JavaScript, not R or Python; the R and Python code starts at layer 3. The page loads the bridge's data file, takes the default view (output (a), Shapley steps, each side's own horizon), finds its two end bars, 'bsz' (BSZ Table 5 row 1) and 'nber' (the NBER expected revenue), and prints their difference as the main estimate, with the two ends in footnote 1. The static page already carries the same three numbers, written by site.R (layer 3), so it reads the same with JavaScript off.
layers.inputs: D = window.__BRIDGE__ from assets/comparison-data.js; B = D.series.own.a.shapley

inputs_from.what: window.__BRIDGE__: every bar of every view; the default view is series.own.a.shapley

layers.outputs: the text '$67.8B' (main estimate), '$103.8B' and '$36.0B' (the two ends)
layers.method_ref: Display only. The definition under the number is the method: the gap on the common output (a) between the bridge's two ends. Footnote 1 says neither side reports it; it is this OPA's reconciliation.

r.symbol: the headline script: read the two end bars, print the gap
r.snippet:
<script src="assets/comparison-data.js"></script>
<script>
  // Read the two ends from the bridge's data file so the number cannot drift from it:
  // the "bsz" and "nber" bars of the default view, output (a), own horizons.
  (function () {
    var D = window.__BRIDGE__;
    if (!D || !D.series || !D.series.own) return;
    var B = D.series.own.a.shapley;
    function end(id) { return B.filter(function (b) { return b.id === id; })[0].value; }
    var bsz = end("bsz"), nber = end("nber");
    document.getElementById("hl-main").textContent = "$" + (bsz - nber).toFixed(1) + "B";
    document.getElementById("hl-bsz").textContent = "$" + bsz.toFixed(1) + "B";
    document.getElementById("hl-nber").textContent = "$" + nber.toFixed(1) + "B";
  })();
</script>

layers.name: The bridge's ends and steps
layers.what: build_all() estimates everything the page shows. For each horizon setting it estimates the model at the all-BSZ inputs (the BSZ end), runs the two decompositions of layer 5 for outputs (a) and (b), and computes the RJKDC report's own expectations: the SSRN Monte Carlo and the NBER one. Each ends row records the BSZ end, the model at all-RJKDC inputs, the two expectations, the model difference (rauh_residual) and the NBER revision (nber_step).

py.snippet:
def build_all(k):
    sup, rauh = bridge_inputs(k)
    so, oo, d = k["bsz"]["outputs"], k["rjkdc"]["outputs"], k["docs"]
    oi = k["rjkdc"]["inputs"]
    ggss_printed = pick(so, "ggss_headline", "printed_value")
    ra = dict(wt_min=pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min"), wt_max=pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6", "printed_value"),
              baseline=pick(oo, "revenue_baseline", "printed_value"),
              c_min=pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min"), c_max=pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max"),
              r_min=pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), r_max=pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max"))
    na = dict(wt_min=0.0, wt_max=pick(k["rjkdc"]["inputs"], "nber_ceiling_hardcoded"),
              f_min=pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_min"), f_max=pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_max"),
              c_min=ra["c_min"], c_max=ra["c_max"], r_min=ra["r_min"], r_max=ra["r_max"])

    settings = ["own"] + [f"common_{'Inf' if math.isinf(h) else h}" for h in HORIZONS]
    bridge, ends = [], []
    for st in settings:
        s2, r2, players = dict(sup), dict(rauh), list(IDS)
        if st != "own":
            H = math.inf if st.endswith("Inf") else float(st.split("_")[1])
            s2["H"] = r2["H"] = H
            players = [p for p in IDS if p != "horizon"]
        v_sup, v_rauh = score_common(s2), score_common(r2)
        own_r = rauh_ssrn_expectation(**ra, H=r2["H"])
        own_n = rauh_nber_expectation(**na, H=r2["H"])
        for out in ("a", "b"):
            sh = shapley_bridge(s2, r2, players, out)
            sq = sequential_bridge(s2, r2, [p for p in SEQUENTIAL if p in players], out)
            for sid, row, title, kind in STEPS:
                bridge.append({"step_id": sid, "horizon_setting": st, "output": out,
                               "shapley": sh.get(sid, 0.0), "sequential": sq.get(sid, 0.0),
                               "sequential_rank": SEQUENTIAL.index(sid) + 1,
                               "disputes_row": row, "title": title, "kind": kind})
            ends.append({"horizon_setting": st, "output": out,
                         "bsz_model": v_sup[out], "rauh_model": v_rauh[out],
                         "rauh_own": own_r[out], "rauh_residual": own_r[out] - v_rauh[out],
                         "nber_own": own_n[out], "nber_step": own_n[out] - own_r[out]})
    bridge.sort(key=lambda r: (r["horizon_setting"], r["output"], IDS.index(r["step_id"])))

layers.name: Splitting the gap into steps
layers.what: Each step switches one disputed input from the BSZ value to the RJKDC value. Because inputs interact, a step's size depends on when it is switched. shapley_bridge() averages each switch over every order, exactly: it estimates the model at all 2^11 = 2,048 subsets of switched inputs and weights each difference by how many orders produce it. sequential_bridge() switches them in one order, Hoopes's. Both sets of steps add up to the model gap, BSZ end to all-RJKDC end.
layers.inputs: sup, rauh (the two input vectors) and the list of steps

inputs_from.what: score_common(): output (a) or (b) at any mix of the two input vectors
sup and rauh, the two input vectors

layers.other_inputs: step_inputs (which argument each step switches) and sequential_order()
layers.outputs: output (a), own horizon: eleven Shapley steps summing to -52.560 (103.815 to 51.255); the largest is billionaires already departed, -21.293
layers.method_ref: Shapley value, the standard average-over-orders decomposition. test-shapley.R checks the sum in every setting and compares with a brute-force average over orders.

r.snippet:
switch_inputs <- function(sup, rauh, on) {
  x <- sup
  for (st in on) for (nm in step_inputs[[st]]) x[[nm]] <- rauh[[nm]]
  x
}

# Exact Shapley values by enumerating all 2^n coalitions (n = 11: 2,048 scorings).
# `players` can exclude steps (e.g. the horizon when both ends share one horizon).
shapley_bridge <- function(sup, rauh, players, output = c("a", "b")) {
  output <- match.arg(output)
  n <- length(players)
  masks <- 0:(2^n - 1)
  inset <- function(mask) players[bitwAnd(mask, 2^(0:(n - 1))) > 0]
  v <- vapply(masks, function(mk) score_common(switch_inputs(sup, rauh, inset(mk)))[[output]], 0)
  size <- vapply(masks, function(mk) sum(bitwAnd(mk, 2^(0:(n - 1))) > 0), 0)
  # weight of a coalition of `size` others (the full coalition never lacks i)
  w <- ifelse(size < n, factorial(size) * factorial(pmax(n - size - 1, 0)) / factorial(n), 0)
  phi <- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    bit <- 2^(i - 1)
    without <- masks[bitwAnd(masks, bit) == 0]
    sum(w[without + 1] * (v[without + bit + 1] - v[without + 1]))
  }, 0)
  stats::setNames(phi, players)
}

sequential_bridge <- function(sup, rauh, order, output = c("a", "b")) {
  output <- match.arg(output)
  prev <- score_common(sup)[[output]]
  out <- numeric(length(order))
  for (k in seq_along(order)) {
    cur <- score_common(switch_inputs(sup, rauh, order[seq_len(k)]))[[output]]
    out[k] <- cur - prev
    prev <- cur
  }
  stats::setNames(out, order)
}

layers.name: The estimating function and the NBER end
layers.what: score_common() is the one function that estimates both sides. Output (a) is 5% x base x (1 - real-estate share) x (1 - avoidance) x S, where S is the share of the base still taxed after departures and the mobility response. At the all-BSZ inputs S = 1, so (a) = 0.05 x 2,307 x 0.9 = 103.815, BSZ Table 5 row 1. rauh_nber_expectation() (model.R lines 134-138, bridge.py lines 156-160) is the NBER end: the revenue is drawn uniformly between 0 and 72, so its expectation is 36. This is the last layer that computes: the difference of its two outputs is the main estimate.
layers.inputs: x: one input vector (sup at the BSZ end); the NBER Monte Carlo bounds

inputs_from.what: sup: tau 0.05, W_core 2157, W_noncit 150, re 0, alpha 0.10, d_conf 0, ...

layers.other_inputs: the NBER bounds wt_min = 0 (a literal in build.R) and wt_max = 72 (contract row nber_ceiling_hardcoded)
layers.method_ref: BSZ PDF p.24 (90% x 5% x $2,307B) and Table 5 row 1, p.39; Jaros and Rauh NBER c15504, the Monte Carlo in the authors' public repository (NPV_dist_v8.R). test-endpoints.R checks both ends against the printed numbers.

r.snippet:
score_common <- function(x) {
  R0  <- x$tau * (x$W_core + x$W_noncit) * (1 - x$re)
  S   <- 1 - (x$d_conf + max(x$d_conf, x$eps * x$dtau)) / 2
  WT  <- R0 * (1 - x$alpha) * S
  X   <- WT * x$s * x$g * x$t_cg
  f   <- x$alpha * x$m + x$kappa * (1 - S) * (1 - x$alpha * x$m)
  A   <- expected_annuity(x$H, x$r_min, x$r_max)
  PV  <- f * x$C * A
  c(a = WT, b = WT + X - PV, R0 = R0, S = S, X = X, f = f, annual_loss = f * x$C,
    annuity = A, PV = PV)
}

layers.name: The two input vectors
layers.what: bridge_inputs() builds the two settings of every disputed input, each value read from a contract row or a transcribed document input. The BSZ base is the contract's 2,307 split into 150 of non-US-citizen residents (GGSS p.2 fn.1) and the rest; the RJKDC values come from the RJKDC contract's workbook sums and Monte Carlo ranges.
layers.inputs: k: the two contracts and the document inputs

inputs_from.what: k$bsz, k$rjkdc (inputs and outputs tables) and k$docs, looked up row by row with pick()

layers.outputs: sup: W_core 2157, W_noncit 150, alpha 0.10, re 0, d_conf 0, dtau 0, ...; rauh: W_core 1894.8, W_noncit 0, alpha 0, dtau 0.05, ...
layers.method_ref: Each value's source and page is in comparison/export/r/inputs.csv (bridge_input_table()).

r.snippet:
bridge_inputs <- function(k) {
  si <- k$bsz$inputs; so <- k$bsz$outputs
  oi <- k$rjkdc$inputs;   oo <- k$rjkdc$outputs
  d  <- k$docs
  W0      <- pick(si, "baseline_net_worth")
  noncit  <- pick(d, "ggss_noncitizen_wealth")
  C_sup   <- pick(si, "ca_inctax_billionaires")
  kappa_s <- (pick(si, "leavers_annual_inctax") / pick(si, "leavers_wealth")) / (C_sup / W0)
  tau     <- pick(oi, "tax_rate")
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(tau, pick(si, "tax_rate"))))
  base_r  <- pick(oi, "baseline_net_worth")
  R0_r    <- pick(oo, "revenue_baseline")           # 94.304, the workbook's own sum
  conf6   <- pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6")         # 67.511
  wt_min  <- pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min")              # 35
  shared <- list(tau = tau, m = pick(si, "mobility_share"), g = pick(si, "gains_share"),
                 t_cg = pick(si, "ca_cg_rate"),
                 r_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), r_max = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max"))
  sup <- c(shared, list(
    W_noncit = noncit, W_core = W0 - noncit, re = 0, d_conf = 0,
    alpha = pick(si, "avoidance_rate"), dtau = 0, eps = pick(si, "semi_elasticity_permanent"),
    kappa = kappa_s, C = C_sup, H = pick(d, "bsz_loss_horizon"),
    s = pick(si, "sell_share")))
  rauh <- c(shared, list(
    W_noncit = 0, W_core = base_r, re = 1 - R0_r / (tau * base_r),
    d_conf = 1 - conf6 / R0_r, alpha = 0, dtau = tau,
    eps = (1 - wt_min / R0_r) / tau,
    kappa = 1, C = (pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min") + pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max")) / 2,
    H = pick(d, "rauh_loss_horizon"), s = 0))
  list(sup = sup, rauh = rauh)
}

def bridge_inputs(k):
    si, so = k["bsz"]["inputs"], k["bsz"]["outputs"]
    oi, oo = k["rjkdc"]["inputs"], k["rjkdc"]["outputs"]
    d = k["docs"]
    W0 = pick(si, "baseline_net_worth")
    noncit = pick(d, "ggss_noncitizen_wealth")
    C_sup = pick(si, "ca_inctax_billionaires")
    kappa_s = (pick(si, "leavers_annual_inctax") / pick(si, "leavers_wealth")) / (C_sup / W0)
    tau = pick(oi, "tax_rate")
    assert abs(tau - pick(si, "tax_rate")) < 1e-12
    base_r = pick(oi, "baseline_net_worth")
    R0_r = pick(oo, "revenue_baseline")
    conf6 = pick(oo, "revenue_confirmed6")
    wt_min = pick(oi, "rauh_mc_wt_min")
    shared = {"tau": tau, "m": pick(si, "mobility_share"), "g": pick(si, "gains_share"),
              "t_cg": pick(si, "ca_cg_rate"),
              "r_min": pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_min"), "r_max": pick(oi, "rauh_mc_r_max")}
    sup = dict(shared, W_noncit=noncit, W_core=W0 - noncit, re=0.0, d_conf=0.0,
               alpha=pick(si, "avoidance_rate"), dtau=0.0,
               eps=pick(si, "semi_elasticity_permanent"), kappa=kappa_s, C=C_sup,
               H=pick(d, "bsz_loss_horizon"), s=pick(si, "sell_share"))
    rauh = dict(shared, W_noncit=0.0, W_core=base_r, re=1 - R0_r / (tau * base_r),
                d_conf=1 - conf6 / R0_r, alpha=0.0, dtau=tau, eps=(1 - wt_min / R0_r) / tau,
                kappa=1.0, C=(pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_min") + pick(oi, "rauh_mc_c_max")) / 2,
                H=pick(d, "rauh_loss_horizon"), s=0.0)

read_contracts <- function(root = comparison_root()) {
  side <- function(s) list(
    inputs  = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, s, "export", "r", "inputs.csv")),
    outputs = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, s, "export", "r", "outputs.csv")))
  docs <- read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "data", "document-inputs.csv"))
  docs$value <- as.numeric(docs$value)          # "Inf" parses to Inf
  list(bsz = side("bsz-analysis"),
       rjkdc = side("rjkdc-analysis"),
       docs       = docs,
       hoopes     = read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "data", "hoopes-fig2.csv")))
}

# Look up one value, failing loudly if the contract row is missing or duplicated.
pick <- function(df, id, col = "value", key = NULL) {
  key <- key %||% names(df)[1]
  hit <- df[df[[key]] == id, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(hit) != 1) stop(sprintf("expected exactly one row '%s', found %d", id, nrow(hit)))
  hit[[col]]
}
